transcript: Are The Bennet Girls Ok? is Bedlam's latest look at a classic, and it might be their best production yet. Adapted by Emily Breeze from the novel Pride and Prejudice, it revolves around five sisters and their mother who's made it her life's mission to get at least one of them married off into a family that can support them. I think I'm the ideal candidate for an audience member, as I'm familiar with the novel, but I'm not a purist about it. This was helpful because although the events of the plot are made clear in this production, there's little to no time spent breaking down all the background information about the circumstances of the Bennet sisters. And as a casual fan of the novel, I was able to notice the plot changes without being resistant to them — some folks might find them hard to swallow. But with this being such a beloved story, it's hard to please everyone, and I think they did a great job. This version has a clear vision and tone that makes the choices feel cohesive, even if they're not what you would expect. And the creative liberties that are taken contribute to a neurotic energy that underscores the entire production. The characters are brash and unsteady, and they notably use contemporary speech, which the title subtly indicates. I found this equally hilarious and endearing, as the youthfulness of these characters is captured nicely. The sisters are sarcastic, dramatic, awkward, and like many teenagers, headstrong. It makes the moments when they really let their guards down feel especially cathartic. You laugh with them and you feel for them, for it's made clear that these characters are so young to be carrying the weight of society's pressures regarding marriage and the social standing of their entire family. And for me, that's the thesis of this production and why the answer to the title is no. Brought to life by a really well-cast ensemble of nine, Are The Bennet Girls Ok? is a great example of a theatrical adaptation that pays homage while furthering the conversation in ways the only theater can do. With that, another program for my collection.
